subject: Post-discovery: schedule tech deep-dive & capacity profile
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Rivera <jordan.rivera@quantaflow.com>, Samira Khan <samira.k@quantaflow.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Sep 2027 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Post-discovery: schedule tech deep-dive & capacity profile

Hi Jordan / Samira —

Thanks again for the productive discovery call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can lock the technical deep-dive (dedicated capacity sizing) — goal is to align on QPS/concurrency, latency SLOs, and a representative load profile so we can size a dedicated GPU pool for your inference traffic.

Immediate asks from your side before the call:
- Confirm 3 preferred 60–90 minute windows next week (we can accommodate cross-ET).
- Share peak and steady-state concurrency (est. users/connections), expected request-per-second (RPS) at peak, and average session length.
- Provide any SLO targets (p50/p95/p99) and acceptance criteria for tail latency.
- If available, attach a small set of sample payloads (JSONL) and an example prompt series to validate tokenization and typical sequence lengths.

I attached a short capacity questionnaire and an examples file to make this easier. On our side Ben will cover inferred GPU footprint and Marcus will bring the runbook for KV/prefix caching behavior.

Proposed slots (Pacific):
- Mon 13 Sep, 09:00–10:30 PT
- Tue 14 Sep, 13:00–14:30 PT
- Wed 15 Sep, 15:00–16:30 PT

If none of those work, tell us two windows that do and we will send a calendar invite.

Thanks — looking forward to the sizing conversation.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: capacity_questionnaire.xlsx (spreadsheet, 6 questions), sample_payload_examples.jsonl (10 small samples), integration_requirements_v1.pdf (2-page checklist)

From: Jordan Rivera <jordan.rivera@quantaflow.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Samira Khan <samira.k@quantaflow.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Sep 2027 17:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-discovery: schedule tech deep-dive & capacity profile

Grace — thanks for the summary and the materials. Samira and I talked offline and we can do Tue 14 Sep at 13:00 PT (that slot works best).

Quick answers to the checklist we can send now while we prepare the payloads:
- Peak RPS: ~120 requests/sec sustained for 15–20 minute bursts during batch ingestion windows; baseline sustained is ~8–10 RPS.
- Concurrency: ~40 concurrent inference streams at peak (each stream issues short sequences ~3–5 messages).
- Typical sequence length (tokens): median 120 tokens; 95th ~560 tokens (with occasional longer analytical prompts).
- Latency targets: p95 < 300ms, p99 < 700ms for API response times; tail accuracy matters for p99.
- Model family: planning to use an open decoder model in the 13–20B range; we may test a quantized variant.

We'll upload a 10–20 sample JSONL file by end of day Monday and fill the questionnaire — Samira will take point on that. Also, is there anything you need around auth (we use mTLS internally) or private VPC peering details before the call?

Jordan
Director of ML Engineering
QuantaFlow

In advance of the call I've attached:
- capacity_questionnaire.xlsx (please complete the shaded cells)
- sample_payload_examples.jsonl (drop-in examples you can replace with your own)
- integration_requirements_v1.pdf (high level network/auth checklist)

Specific asks for the sizing session so we can do live validation:
- If possible, include a short replay or log that shows a 5–10 minute high-intensity burst (we'll use that to estimate batching behavior and KV cache hit rate).
- Confirm whether you will require private deployment (VPC peering) or hosted with dedicated pool — if VPC, please share the rough network egress constraints.
- If your team runs an internal rate limiter or gateway, note its burst token behavior and warm-up period (this affects cold-start sizing).

Calendar invite: https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=abcd1234efgh

We'll cover: workload validation, target model & quantization profile, candidate GPU types, and a recommended reservoir/burst plan for the dedicated pool. Marcus will demo a short KV-cache diagnostic script and Ben will present a cost/latency tradeoff table.

Talk soon — appreciate the quick turn.

Best,
Grace
